correctness.rationale: A coordinate vector has norm max(1,1/s), while its normalized Hadamard image has norm max(1/√n,√n/s); equality is impossible for s<1 and forces s=√n otherwise. At n=2 the eight vertices (±1,±(√2−1)) and their swaps are permuted by the standard Hadamard reflection and signed coordinate permutations. At n=4 the orthant polytopes have zero-one vertices of support at most two; zero and singleton supports are nonextreme in the full symmetric ball. Each two-support signed vector is extreme: the two saturated cube coordinates and the ℓ₁ constraint force any endpoints of a midpoint representation to be that vector. Any pair of Hadamard columns agree on exactly two rows and disagree on two, so the normalized transform permutes the 24 vertices. For three distinct columns h_i,h_j,h_k, orthogonality makes the rowwise pairs (h_i h_j,h_i h_k) uniformly distributed over the four sign patterns, since all three nonconstant sign characters sum to zero. Thus U(e_i+e_j+e_k) has absolute coordinate 3/√n on n/4 rows and 1/√n on the rest. At s=√n this gives output norm 3/2 and input norm max(1,3/√n), yielding exactly the claimed lower bounds on the operator norm. The same pattern proves the Hadamard order divisibility used to exclude intervening dimensions, without asserting existence. check.py was inspected, not executed; its Sylvester tests do not establish arbitrary-Hadamard quantifiers.

evidence: At s=√n the polar vertices are the signed coordinates and the cube sign vectors scaled by 1/√n. For n>4 each cube vertex has another vertex at distance 2/√n, but a coordinate vertex has no vertex that close: its nearest cube-vertex distance is √(2−2/√n). An orthogonal normalized Hadamard sends a coordinate vertex to a cube vertex, ruling out preservation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This credits a short route from known geometry to the qualitative failure and does not count that alone as the distinct contribution. The explicit √2 or 3/2 lower bound evaluates a primal witness using the uniform three-column sign pattern; the qualitative polar-distance obstruction and the rounding optimum do not give those inequalities.
